title: Tenant-aware region & tier routing constraints for safer hosted spillover
creator: Amina Patel
description:
Problem: During recent peak periods we observed tenant traffic spilling from Dedicated pools into Hosted which caused noisy neighbors and degraded p95 for a small set of latency-sensitive customers. Existing routing rules are global and prioritize overall throughput; they lack per-tenant budgets, per-region hard caps, and safe downgrade behavior when the only available hosted variants are incompatible with tenant SLAs.

Goal: Add tenant-aware constraints and safeguards to the smart router so spillover is predictable and safe. This ticket scopes the control-plane and runtime policy changes required to: define per-tenant spillover budgets, enforce region affinity constraints, gate tier-based routing (e.g., enterprise vs community), and add an emergency circuit-breaker that routes to specified fallback model variants or throttles requests rather than silently failing over to incompatible hosted models.

Why this is different: Prior tickets focused on global guardrails and tier routing. This work is tenant-scoped: every customer can express a small set of invariants (max_spillover_tokens_per_minute, preferred_regions, forbidden_regions, allowed_fallback_variants, latency_threshold_ms) which the router will respect. Implementing this requires changes to allocation decision logic, config surface in Console, and a fast-path in the runtime to check per-request tenancy constraints without adding significant latency.
acceptance_criteria: Router supports per-tenant config keys: max_spillover_qps, allowed_regions, region_preference_order, allowed_fallbacks, and emergency_throttle_pct.
Requests for tenants with explicit allowed_regions must not be routed to hosts outside the set unless operator override is active; unit and integration tests validate enforcement.
Per-tenant spillover budget tracking implemented in the control plane with >= 99% correctness under 50k rps in load test; observed token accounting matches simulated usage.

Emergency circuit-breaker triggers when hosted latency > tenant latency_threshold_ms or spillover budget exhausted: behavior must be configurable to (a) throttle, (b) route to a quantized compatible variant, or (c) return 503 with informative error.
Console exposes a tenant routing view and edit form for the new keys; changes are audited and roll back within 2 minutes if validation fails.
End-to-end performance impact on median routing latency < 2ms and p99 impact < 5ms compared to baseline; benchmarking artifacts attached.
Documentation (docs.redwood.io + internal runbook) updated with examples and migration notes for large customers.
tasks: Design: finalize tenant config schema and validation rules (owner: Amina).
API: add control-plane endpoints for CRUD of tenant routing constraints (owner: Jorge).
Router: implement fast-path tenant checks in routing decision code with caching (owner: Priya).
Runtime: add fallback selection logic for quantized/compatible variants and emergency throttle hooks (owner: Marcus).
Console: add UI for per-tenant routing settings and audit trail (owner: Lina).
QA: load-test with mixed enterprise/community tenants at 50k rps and verify billing/metrics (owner: QA team).
Docs + Runbook: publish migration guide and incident playbook for misconfigurations (owner: Technical Writing).
tradeoffs: Per-tenant checks increase control-plane complexity and state to sync; we mitigate by making tenant configs small and cacheable at edge routers with TTLs.
Strict region enforcement can reduce global utilization and raise cost; we will offer operator-set overrides and an opt-in conservative mode for large customers.

Choosing to throttle vs return 503 has product implications: throttling preserves partial availability but may increase latency; returning 503 is explicit and simple. We'll default to safe (503) for P0 tenants and throttling for P1/P2 with clear docs.
Fallback to quantized variants may introduce quality regressions; acceptance criteria require model evaluation on representative prompt sets before enabling per-tenant allowed_fallbacks.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Deploy tenant config API and router checks to canary region. Enable for internal tenants only; collect metrics for 48 hours.
Phase 2 (pilot): Enable for 3 willing enterprise customers with explicit contracts and monitored dashboards; validate billing, latency, and QA prompts.
Phase 3 (general release): Expose Console UI, defaulting to conservative settings for new tenants. Provide migration script for existing tenants relying on global policies.
Rollback: feature flag to disable tenant checks at router layer; documented runbook for emergency rollback with <5 minute recovery target.
